findings.title: Invalid ERB Ruby prevents existing discussions from rendering
findings.body: The opening `if` is closed with `end if`, leaving a trailing `if` without a condition. Rails cannot compile this template, so requests for an existing embedded topic fail with a template syntax error instead of displaying the discussion. Close the block with `end`.

findings.title: Sanitize imported HTML before storing it as cooked content
findings.body: Feed content reaches this method without HTML sanitization, and the post is created with `raw_html`, which makes `Post#cook` return the HTML unchanged. `absolutize_urls` only parses and rewrites URLs; it does not remove scripts, event handlers, or dangerous URL schemes. Consequently, malicious HTML in a feed becomes stored executable content on the forum's origin. Sanitize both initial imports and revisions before bypassing the normal cooking pipeline.

findings.title: Validate redirect destinations before fetching embedded pages
findings.body: The request-driven retrieval path checks only the hostname of the original embed URL, then uses `open(url)`, which follows HTTP redirects. An allowed-host URL that redirects to another host can therefore make the worker fetch internal services or attacker-controlled content despite the hostname restriction. Validate the scheme, port, resolved address, and each redirect destination before fetching rather than relying solely on the initial host check.

findings.title: Handle RSS entries that use description or content:encoded
findings.body: The poller assumes every item has a non-nil `content` field. Ordinary RSS feeds commonly provide the body through `description` or `content:encoded` instead, so `i.content.scrub` raises for those entries. This aborts the entire polling run, preventing the entry and all subsequent entries from importing. Select the supported body fields with a fallback and handle missing bodies explicitly.

findings.title: Resolve relative URLs with URI joining instead of prefix concatenation
findings.body: The URL rewriting handles only values starting with `/` and treats protocol-relative URLs as local paths. For example, `//cdn.example.com/image.jpg` becomes `http://article-host/cdn.example.com/image.jpg`, while `images/photo.jpg` remains relative to the forum rather than the source article. The same problem affects links. Resolve references against the source URL with URI joining so imported images and links continue to point to their original destinations.
